accuracy.evidence: Matches NC Y5 Geometry (identify 3-D shapes from 2-D representations) and standard KS2/KS3 nets content: 6 faces on a cube, 11 distinct cube nets, row-of-6 and 2×3 block are not nets, cuboid nets need matching rectangles, cylinder net is rectangle + two circles, triangular prism has 2 triangles + 3 rectangles. Tabs are not faces.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets 'any 6 squares make a cube net', counting tabs as faces, 7-square 'nets', and ignoring edge-length match on cuboids. Adult notes and Challenge why() cover four/eight/yes/face/one/six/col.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagnets folds a cross cube net, rejects row and 2×3, builds a cuboid net from named rectangles, and matches cube/cuboid/triangular-prism nets. flagsolid teaches naming solids and faces, not nets. Distinct mechanism.

lab_teaches.evidence: Folding counts to 6, rejecting false patterns, placing matching faces, then matching net→solid. Discovery then confirmation; Show-me walks each task.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions: 6 faces; row of 6 fails; cuboid needs matching rectangles; 2 triangles + 3 rectangles → triangular prism. Wrong options are real slips.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven items with tagged wrongs and specific why() text for face-count, false nets, tab mistakes and cuboid edge matching.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and concrete cardboard-box images for ages 8–11. Adult names NC Y5/Y6 wording without filler.

no_filler.evidence: No banned filler. Every line defines nets, tests them, or names a mistake.

mobile.evidence: young class, button twins for fold/reject/place/match, large square cells, three-band tap targets on reject and match steps.

accessibility.evidence: Button twins for every action; live aria-label; challenge as buttons with aria-live feedback.

sources: National Curriculum in England: mathematics — Year 5 Geometry (identify 3-D shapes from 2-D representations); Year 6 / KS3 nets
